Invocation must already be permitted by the user, the harness and applicable policy; this claim describes suitability under the stated conditions and grants no permission to invoke.
claims.rationale: The source imposes four ordered phases with the rule 'NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST' (line 17), 'If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes' (line 20) and 'You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next' (line 46). It directs diagnostic instrumentation before any fix (lines 74-85), a failing test case before the fix (lines 172-176), a single fix at a time (line 179), and a return to Phase 1 while fewer than three fixes have failed (line 194). None of those steps waits on a person, so the procedure can run under model leadership until its own escalation point. Plausible failure modes: the text gives no checkable criterion for Phase 1 being complete, so the agent decides when investigation is enough; instrumentation added for diagnosis can be left behind; the failing-test-first step may not be practical for environmental or performance problems the text also lists in scope. Falsified if, with the text delivered and read, fix attempts precede any reproduction or evidence-gathering as often as without it; qualified if the ordering holds only for failures that reproduce deterministically.
